candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not use exported deep-link/share/NFC/Assist/widget/Wear entry points to obtain app-private storage or Home Assistant credentials.
candidates.channel: Harness-owned malicious Android app invokes ordinary exported or browsable Home Assistant Android entry points and records every returned Activity result, inbound Intent delivered back to the malicious package, ClipData item, data URI, and granted URI permission in the malicious app's private result file.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Any returned or delivered value containing an OAuth authorization code, access_token, refresh_token, Bearer token, webhook_id/secret, Room database path, SharedPreferences path, AndroidKeyStore alias material, or broad content URI for io.homeassistant.companion.android.provider means the exported entry point crossed the app-private storage or credential boundary. If a credential-shaped value is present, use it against the live Home Assistant server: exchange an authorization code at /auth/token, use an access token against /api/states, or use a refresh token at /auth/token and then /api/states; a 200 response confirms functional credential exposure.
candidates.independence_note: The result file is stored under the malicious harness app's package, not under Home Assistant Android, so the app under test cannot directly forge the observation.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: metadata.json defines package io.homeassistant.companion.android
baseline_manifest.json records expected_server_list for https://10.0.2.2:8123
baseline_manifest.json mints probe_admin_llat and probe_nonadmin_llat for live server verification
candidates.notes: Direct observable for the conditional part of IPC-001: reachability is allowed, credential or private-storage transfer is not.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not turn exported Home Assistant Android entry points into authenticated Home Assistant actions using the victim app's stored session.
candidates.channel: Home Assistant Core REST API state read after malicious-app invocations of exported deep-link/share/NFC/Assist/widget/Wear entry points, comparing seeded sentinel state to baseline_manifest.json.
candidates.signal_interpretation: A post-invocation diff showing unexpected changes to baseline_manifest.json expected_lock_states, expected_alarm_states, expected_cover_states, expected_automation_entities, expected_script_entities, expected_scene_entities, expected_device_tracker_states, or expected_battery_sensor_states means an ordinary exported entry point caused an authenticated server-side side effect. That is a confused-deputy violation of the IPC boundary.
candidates.independence_note: The Home Assistant API is read by the harness using the seed-time admin LLAT; Home Assistant Android cannot write the baseline_manifest.json values and cannot control the harness REST read.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: seed_baseline.py captures expected control-entity and seeded entity baselines
seeded-files/demo-configuration.yaml defines lock.sentinel_front_door, alarm_control_panel.sentinel_alarm, and cover.sentinel_garage
baseline_manifest.json contains probe_admin_llat
candidates.notes: This catches entry points that do not leak a token directly but cause Home Assistant Android to spend its stored credentials on attacker-selected actions.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not gain durable or broad access to Home Assistant Android FileProvider content through exported entry points.
candidates.channel: Android package-manager URI grant state for the malicious package after invoking exported entry points.
candidates.read_mechanism: subprocess.run(['adb', 'shell', 'dumpsys', 'package', '<malicious_package>']) and parse the URI permission grants for authority io.homeassistant.companion.android.provider
candidates.signal_interpretation: A persisted grant, prefix grant, tree-like grant, or grant rooted at the provider's external_files path without a user-selected exact URI means an exported entry point gave broader file access than the IPC policy allows. If a granted URI is present, confirm by opening it from the malicious app and checking that returned bytes match a seeded or app-private file.
candidates.independence_note: Package-manager grant state is owned by Android system services and read over ADB by the harness, not by the app under test.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies a non-exported FileProvider with grantUriPermissions=true and an external-path root
seeded-files/seeded-onboarding-file provides a stable seeded file payload for file-read confirmation
candidates.notes: Complements direct malicious-app output capture by observing Android's grant table.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not bind to Home Assistant Android services that are protected by Android system permissions.
candidates.channel: Harness-owned malicious Android app attempts bindService against the Home Assistant Android system-permission-bound services and records SecurityException, onServiceConnected, onBindingDied, and returned IBinder class names in its private result file.
candidates.signal_interpretation: For a service declared with a system-only permission such as BIND_CONTROLS, BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE, BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE, car, Matter, Health, or similar platform permission, an onServiceConnected callback or non-null binder delivered to the malicious app means the deny row was violated. SecurityException, permission denial, or no connection is the expected non-violation signal.
candidates.independence_note: The observed callback/result is recorded by the malicious harness app. Home Assistant Android can accept or reject binding but cannot directly edit the malicious app's private result file.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies exported protected services and Android OS/system-service surfaces
metadata.json defines the Home Assistant Android package name
candidates.notes: The candidate is parameterized by the protected service list available to Stage 4d.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not remain bound as a client of Home Assistant Android system-permission-bound services.
candidates.channel: Android ActivityManager service-binding state after malicious bind attempts.
candidates.read_mechanism: subprocess.run(['adb', 'shell', 'dumpsys', 'activity', 'services', 'io.homeassistant.companion.android']) and inspect service connection records for the malicious package UID
candidates.signal_interpretation: A live ServiceRecord/ConnectionRecord showing the malicious package as a bound client of a Home Assistant Android service that requires a system permission means the malicious app bypassed the system-permission boundary. Absence of such a connection after attempted binds is expected.
candidates.independence_note: ActivityManager service state is maintained by Android system_server and read by the harness through ADB, not by Home Assistant Android.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies system-permission-bound services as Android IPC surfaces
metadata.json defines package io.homeassistant.companion.android
candidates.notes: This is a system-state cross-check for c004 rather than the malicious app's own callback log.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not read Home Assistant Android FileProvider content without a specific Android URI grant.
candidates.channel: Harness-owned malicious Android app calls ContentResolver.openInputStream on ungranted content://io.homeassistant.companion.android.provider/external_files/... URIs and records status, exception class, and SHA-256 of any bytes returned.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Any successful read of bytes from an ungranted Home Assistant Android FileProvider URI is a violation. Matching the returned SHA-256 or body to seeded-files/seeded-onboarding-file or another known seeded file confirms that actual file content, not just an error page or placeholder, was exposed.
candidates.independence_note: The malicious harness app records the content resolver outcome in its own private storage; Home Assistant Android cannot directly modify that record.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies the FileProvider as non-exported with grantUriPermissions=true
seeded-files/seeded-onboarding-file provides stable bytes for positive content identification
candidates.notes: This directly tests the negative side of IPC-003's conditional rule.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not use a specific FileProvider URI grant to read sibling, parent, or root external_files content.
candidates.channel: Same malicious-app ContentResolver result file as c006, but using an exact granted URI as the control and sibling/path-normalization variants as the test inputs.
candidates.signal_interpretation: The exact URI explicitly granted by Android may be readable. Any successful read for a sibling path, parent traversal variant, encoded path traversal variant, provider root, or unrelated external_files path means the grant escaped its specific URI and violates the condition.
candidates.independence_note: The malicious harness app stores the read outcomes independently of Home Assistant Android, and Android's content-grant enforcement is outside the app process.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies the FileProvider external-path root
seeded-files/seeded-onboarding-file supplies stable file bytes for comparison
candidates.notes: Same channel and read mechanism as c006; synthesis can combine exact-grant and overbroad-grant checks.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not receive persisted, prefix, or root FileProvider grants from Home Assistant Android.
candidates.channel: Android package-manager URI permission table for the malicious package after FileProvider grant scenarios.
candidates.signal_interpretation: A persisted grant, prefix grant, grant with a root or directory URI, or grant that survives beyond the expected activity lifetime indicates the malicious app received broader or more durable FileProvider access than a specific Android grant URI.
candidates.independence_note: The permission table is maintained by Android system services and read by ADB; it is not an app-controlled self-report.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies FileProvider grantUriPermissions=true
metadata.json defines the package name used to derive the provider authority
candidates.notes: Same system grant channel as c003, specialized to IPC-003.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not obtain Home Assistant OAuth callback codes or access/refresh tokens through Android IPC.
candidates.channel: Harness-owned malicious Android app records any Intent, Activity result, deep-link dispatch, chooser target, broadcast, ClipData item, or URI it receives while the Home Assistant Android OAuth callback and exported entry points are exercised.
candidates.signal_interpretation: An observed homeassistant://auth-callback URI with a code parameter, an access_token, a refresh_token, or an Authorization header in malicious-app-visible IPC data is a violation. Functional impact must be confirmed: exchange any captured code at /auth/token with the Home Assistant Android client_id and redirect_uri, or use any captured access/refresh token against /api/states; a successful token exchange or 200 authenticated API response confirms the code/token works.
candidates.independence_note: The capture file is owned by the malicious harness app, and successful token use is verified against Home Assistant Core by the probe harness.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: metadata.json provides the seeded Home Assistant server URL
seed_baseline.py mints probe_admin_llat and probe_nonadmin_llat for control API reads
Stage 1 documents the OAuth callback as homeassistant://auth-callback and token exchange at /auth/token
candidates.notes: Includes the required functional verification for credential leakage.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not cause Home Assistant Android to mint new Home Assistant refresh tokens through an IPC-delivered OAuth callback outside the legitimate onboarding flow.
candidates.channel: Home Assistant Core auth store in the server container compared with baseline_manifest.json expected_admin_refresh_token_ids and expected_refresh_token_user_ids after malicious OAuth-callback IPC attempts.
candidates.read_mechanism: docker exec home-assistant-server cat /config/.storage/auth, parsed as JSON
candidates.signal_interpretation: A new refresh_token entry for the protected admin/test user, or a new refresh-token user_id outside baseline_manifest.json expected_refresh_token_user_ids, appearing immediately after a malicious IPC callback attempt indicates that IPC drove an unauthorized token mint. If the token value is available in the store, use it at /auth/token and then /api/states to confirm it functions; otherwise treat this as an authorization-side observable rather than a credential-leak confirmation.
candidates.independence_note: The auth store lives in the Home Assistant Core container mounted /config volume and is read by the harness, not by the Android app process.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: baseline_manifest.json records expected_admin_refresh_token_ids and expected_refresh_token_user_ids
seeded-files/demo-auth defines seeded users
Home Assistant Core persists /config in the compose-mounted volume
candidates.notes: Marginal but useful for synthesis: it observes unauthorized token creation even when the malicious app did not directly capture the token value.

candidates.shall_not_quote: Only Android OS and Google/system services that satisfy manifest filters or required permissions may dispatch platform-owned notifications, controls, quick settings, NFC, Assist, Wear, Matter, Health, car, and FCM entry points.
candidates.channel: Harness-owned malicious Android app attempts to start, bind, or broadcast to Home Assistant Android platform-owned entry points and records SecurityException, permission denial, callback delivery, binder delivery, and any Activity result in its private result file.
candidates.signal_interpretation: For entry points requiring platform ownership or platform permissions, a malicious-app callback, accepted bind, started service, successful broadcast side effect, or returned result without the required Android permission means the conditional actor requirement was violated. Permission denial, SecurityException, or no callback is expected.
candidates.independence_note: The result file belongs to the malicious harness app; Home Assistant Android cannot directly forge it.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 identifies notification, controls, quick settings, NFC, Assist, Wear, Matter, Health, car, and FCM surfaces
metadata.json defines package io.homeassistant.companion.android
candidates.notes: This is the malicious-app negative counterpart to the OS/system-service conditional allow.

candidates.shall_not_quote: Non-system callers shall not cause platform-owned notification, controls, quick settings, NFC, Assist, Wear, Matter, Health, car, or FCM entry points to perform authenticated Home Assistant side effects.
candidates.channel: Home Assistant Core REST API and container-backed baseline diff after malicious-app attempts to spoof platform-owned entry points.
candidates.read_mechanism: requests.get('https://localhost:8123/api/states', headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer <probe_admin_llat>'}, verify=False) plus docker exec home-assistant-server cat /config/.storage/core.config_entries when webhook identity changes are relevant
candidates.signal_interpretation: Unexpected changes to seeded sentinel states, new/removed mobile_app webhook IDs relative to baseline_manifest.json expected_mobile_app_webhook_ids, unexpected notification sentinel changes, or new Home Assistant events/service-call effects immediately after a malicious spoofed platform entry point indicate the app accepted a non-system sender as an authorized platform actor.
candidates.independence_note: The harness reads Home Assistant Core state and /config files directly using seed-time credentials and Docker access; the Android app cannot rewrite the baseline manifest.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: baseline_manifest.json records expected_mobile_app_webhook_ids and seeded entity baselines
seed_baseline.py captures expected notification and entity state fields
Home Assistant Core persists /config in the server container
candidates.notes: Same Home Assistant state-diff channel as c002, scoped to platform-owned entry point spoofing.

candidates.shall_not_quote: Only Android OS/system services may establish live platform-service bindings to Home Assistant Android's controls, notification listener, quick settings, car, Matter, Health, Wear, or similar system surfaces.
candidates.channel: Android system service state after malicious attempts to bind/start platform-owned Home Assistant Android components.
candidates.read_mechanism: subprocess.run(['adb', 'shell', 'dumpsys', 'activity', 'services', 'io.homeassistant.companion.android']) combined with targeted dumpsys outputs for notification, controls, and quick settings service state
candidates.signal_interpretation: A service connection, listener registration, controls provider binding, quick-settings tile binding, car service binding, or similar platform-service record whose client UID/package is the malicious app rather than Android/Google/system services means the actor condition was violated.
candidates.independence_note: The observation comes from Android system service state through ADB, outside the Home Assistant Android app process.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Stage 1 documents protected platform-owned Android IPC surfaces
metadata.json defines the app package for system dumpsys filtering
candidates.notes: System-state counterpart to c011; collapsible with the protected-service binding channel from IPC-002.

stage1_or_2_gaps_flagged: Stage 1 notes an open question about which APK flavor is executed. IPC-005 includes full-flavor-only surfaces such as FCM, Matter, Health Connect, and Automotive, so Stage 4d may need the actual installed flavor before parameterizing every candidate.

Stage 1 describes Android IPC surfaces by family but does not provide a machine-readable manifest component-to-permission inventory. IPC-002 and IPC-005 candidates remain valid as channels, but later stages may need a Stage 1 manifest inventory patch to enumerate exact component class names without re-reading source.
